summary: v0.3.0 brings God's Eye View down to the street, into your pocket and into three new languages. Open street-level photos from four providers without leaving the globe, use the app on a phone with a layout built for it, and read the interface in Spanish, Russian or Simplified Chinese. Short share links, a rebuilt voice assistant, your own map files, GNSS interference and aircraft emergencies, ten new camera packs and about thirty new bikeshare systems come with it. ## Street Level See the street from the globe (Cameras ▸ Street Level). Coverage lines drape on the terrain and Google 3D tiles; click a street and the nearest photo opens in the panel, flat or 360°, with view cones along its sequence and ‹ › to step through it. - **Four providers, one at a time**: **Panoramax** and **KartaView**, which need no key at all, **Mapillary** with a free client token, and **Google Street View** on the Google 3D map with your Google Maps key. - Every caption names the photo's author and licence and links to the original. - Filter by 360° or flat imagery and by capture date; share links remember the provider and filters. - Host apps can compose their own provider list, and point Mapillary at a server-side Graph endpoint so no token reaches the page. ## On your phone On screens 720 px wide and narrower, the globe stays full screen and a bottom tab bar (Layers, Cameras, Context, Search, More) opens one panel sheet at a time. Swipe a sheet down to close it. - Pinch zoom is three times as responsive, aircraft and ships are easier to tap, and opening Context shows the aircraft you are tracking. - Add it to your home screen: the app ships a web app manifest and icons, so it installs with the God's Eye View mark instead of a blank tile. ## In your language The interface now speaks **Spanish**, **Russian** and **Simplified Chinese**. Pick a language from the globe button in the bottom-right corner, or open the app with `?lang=es`, `?lang=ru` or `?lang=zh-CN`; by default it follows your browser. - Each language is one JSON file keyed by the English text, and `npm test` fails on missing or broken translations, so adding a language is a contained piece of work. ## Also in this release ### Short share links - The share button makes short `/share/` links. The code is a compact, versioned description of the view, so a link opens the same way on any copy of the app, including your own local install. - A link can follow an aircraft, military aircraft or satellite. If it has stopped reporting, the view opens at its last known position and says so. - A mistyped link is refused instead of opening the wrong view, and older long `#v=2` links keep working. - The codec is a package export, so a server can read share links, for example for link previews ([format](https://github.com/bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view/blob/main/docs/SHARE-LINK-FORMAT.md)). ### Voice - **Answers you can trust.** Voice can turn on and query every data layer by its everyday name ("buses", "hurricanes", "military bases"). It counts up to 250,000 records per layer, says when a layer is off or still loading instead of answering zero, and marks partial answers. - **Short spoken answers, details on screen.** A card above the mic shows captions, the steps of a slow request and the result with its sources. - **Point and ask.** Hold Space with the cursor on an aircraft, ship or place and ask "what's that?" or "track that one". - **Gemini Live** as an alternative to OpenAI Realtime, ChatGPT sign-in for OpenAI voice (experimental), a Voice Preview and Settings panel, and globe rotation. ### New on the map - **Your own files.** Import GeoJSON, KML, KMZ and GPX from DISPLAY or drop them on the globe. KML keeps its styles and heights, and the files never leave your device. - **GNSS Integrity** (Events) maps the navigation accuracy aircraft report, which is where GPS interference shows up. It is evidence, not confirmation, and its method and limits are documented. Flights and military flights also highlight **emergency squawks** and ADS-B emergency statuses. - **A real sky**: the 9,096 stars of the Yale Bright Star Catalogue where they are at the scene's time, over a soft Milky Way. - **Air quality** in the Weather group, starting with Canada's AQHI, and **S2 GhostMaps**, S2 Underground's public intel products, updated as new editions are published. - **Scope controls** for the HUD, a cloud-filter slider for satellite clouds, offline `geo:` links in search, and area tools that break results down by airline, country, aircraft type or ship type. ### Cameras, bikes and transit - **Ten new CCTV packs**: Taiwan's national freeways (about 1,800 cameras), Hong Kong (about 1,000), Norway's Statens vegvesen (about 850, with live video for about 135), City of Toronto, Catalonia, Washington State's WSDOT and King County, and opt-in packs for Florida FL511, New York City and Lithuania, whose terms or unconfirmed licences require it. - Cameras with a known model show its datasheet resolution, night vision and field of view, and live-video cameras are coloured apart from stills. - **About thirty new bikeshare systems**: seven Brazilian Bike Itaú cities, Bogotá and Santiago, Toronto, Detroit, Pittsburgh, Aspen and Kona & Hilo, six Norwegian cities, Barcelona's Bicing and AMBici, and nine more Spanish cities. - **Nine Ontario transit feeds**, including TTC, MiWay, HSR and YRT/Viva, with each city's own names for its vehicles and routes. ### Install, performance and security - **Docker**: `docker compose up` runs the app with no local Node install, with a health check and SELinux support. Pinokio now opens the app in your system browser. - **Faster rendering**: aircraft models skip Cesium's per-model environment map (about 2 ms less GPU time per frame with 150 models in view), turned-off layers release their memory, and hidden tabs stop polling. - **Hardening**: cross-site requests are refused and rates limited on the terrain, traffic, Overpass and bikeshare proxies; the remaining upstream reads are size-capped; and dependency CVEs are patched. - **Correctness**: dozens of fixes for the antimeridian, impossible dates, and values that should read as unknown instead of zero, across satellites, fires, cyclones, ships, launches, directions and the HUD. ## 🌟 Summary
v8.4.192 improves compatibility with PyTorch 2.15 and CUDA 13 for multi-GPU training and ONNX Runtime GPU inference, alongside a small update to Platform response documentation.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **More reliable multi-GPU training:** On PyTorch 2.8 and newer, each NCCL process group is explicitly bound to the GPU selected for its training rank. This helps prevent device-mismatch errors, especially when GPUs are selected in a non-default order.
- **More dependable ONNX GPU inference:** Linux CUDA setups now install ONNX Runtime’s CUDA dependencies and preload their libraries, helping prevent a missing cuRAND library from causing inference to fall back to the CPU.
- **Updated CUDA tooling:** The Docker training image now uses PyTorch 2.15, and the export image and GPU CI setup include the required ONNX Runtime CUDA package.
- **Clearer Platform API docs:** Prediction response examples no longer list `metadata.classNames`. Class names remain available on individual detections; dataset and model class names are unchanged.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🖥️ **Fewer multi-GPU training failures** for setups that use GPUs in a custom order or select GPUs dynamically.
- ⚡ **More reliable GPU acceleration for ONNX Runtime** on supported Linux CUDA environments, reducing unintended CPU fallback.
- 🧰 **Better alignment across development, CI, and Docker environments** when using newer PyTorch and CUDA dependencies.
- 📦 **Slightly leaner, more accurate API examples** that match the Platform prediction response.

No model architecture or prediction behavior changes are indicated in this release.

## What's Changed
* Remove classNames from Platform predict response docs by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26919
* Support torch 2.15 CUDA in DDP training and ONNX Runtime inference by @raimbekovm in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26928


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.191...v8.4.192
